items.note: The opening states the decision: keep pgvector on Postgres or move to a dedicated vector database.
States about 5M embeddings at 1536 dimensions, growing about 1M per quarter.
States that the team already runs Postgres 16 on AWS RDS.
States a budget under $500/month and makes it a cost criterion.
States that every query must filter by tenant_id (multi-tenant) and makes tenant-filtered search a criterion.
Says to pick at most 4 options including pgvector, and repeats the limit in the stop rules.
Output asks for a comparison table plus one clear recommendation.
Source rules say to prefer sources from the last 12 months and to flag older ones.
Steps 1 and 3 ask for a wide scan first, then a deep look at the top 2.

invented: The budget is described as "all-in for the vector workload". The person only said under $500/month and did not say what the budget covers.
